concepts.title: Nature of Services: Intangibility and Inseparability
concepts.definition: Services are intangible activities that cannot be stored, touched or separated from their provider, differ from goods on intangibility, inconsistency, inseparability, inventory loss and customer involvement, and banking, insurance, transport, warehousing and communication are the major business services.
concepts.key_idea: A service is performed rather than produced, its quality varies by provider and situation, and it cannot be inventoried for later sale.
question_patterns: distinguish services from goods with examples
explain intangibility and inseparability of services
why can services not be stored in inventory
state the five features that differentiate services from goods
name the major types of business services
how does customer involvement affect service quality

solution_steps.explain: Check whether the offering can be seen or touched.
Apply the five distinguishing features one by one.
Classify the activity as banking, insurance, transport or warehousing.

concepts.title: Banking: Types of Banks and Types of Accounts
concepts.definition: A bank accepts deposits repayable on demand and lends the money, and its types include commercial banks, cooperative banks, central bank and specialised banks, while depositors may hold savings, current, fixed or recurring deposit accounts.
concepts.key_idea: Banks create credit through lending, act as agents for collection and payment, and the Reserve Bank of India supervises them as the central bank.
question_patterns: define a bank and state its functions
differentiate savings account and current account
what is a fixed deposit and a recurring deposit
name the types of banks in India
explain the credit creation function of commercial banks
what services does a bank provide as an agent

solution_steps.explain: Match deposit needs with savings, current, fixed or recurring accounts.
Separate accepting deposits from lending and agency services.
Recall the role of the central bank over commercial banks.

concepts.title: Insurance: Principles and Types
concepts.definition: Insurance is a contract in which the insurer indemnifies the insured against a specified loss in return for premium, resting on principles of utmost good faith, insurable interest, indemnity, contribution, subrogation, mitigation and cause proxima.
concepts.key_idea: Life insurance, fire insurance and marine insurance differ in the nature of risk covered, and the premium is the consideration paid by the insured for the cover.
question_patterns: define insurance and state its principles
explain the principle of utmost good faith with example
differentiate life fire and marine insurance
what is meant by indemnity and subrogation
what is a premium in an insurance contract
how does the principle of insurable interest apply

solution_steps.explain: Confirm premium, insurer, insured and the covered risk.
Test utmost good faith, insurable interest and indemnity in the case.
Place the cover under life, fire or marine insurance.

concepts.title: Transport, Warehousing, Communication and Postal Services
concepts.definition: Transport removes the hindrance of place by carrying goods by road, rail, air or waterways, warehousing removes the hindrance of time by storing goods till demand arises, and communication and postal services link buyers and sellers by moving information.
concepts.key_idea: Warehouses may be private, public, bonded or government, and bonded warehouses let importers store goods until customs duty is paid.
question_patterns: how does transport remove the hindrance of place
define warehousing and name its types
what is a bonded warehouse
state the role of communication in business

explain postal and telecom services for business

solution_steps.explain: Identify place, time or knowledge as the obstacle.
Pair the obstacle with transport, warehousing or communication.
Classify the warehouse or transport mode used.
